title: Stellantis Recalls Nearly One Million Vehicles Over Backup Camera Software Glitch
excerpt: Radio software in 2026-27 Chrysler, Jeep, Dodge and Ram models may prevent rearview cameras from displaying properly; over-the-air fix is forthcoming.
body:
• Stellantis is recalling 955,000 vehicles worldwide — 848,000 in the U.S. — after radio software was found to interfere with rearview camera displays.
  • The recall covers 2026-27 model year Chrysler, Dodge, Jeep and Ram vehicles, with an over-the-air software update expected to fix the issue.
  • No accidents or injuries have been reported, but the company says drivers should use mirrors when reversing until the update is available.

Stellantis announced Monday that it is recalling approximately 955,000 vehicles worldwide after discovering that radio software in certain models can prevent rearview cameras from displaying images properly — a defect that violates federal safety standards requiring rear visibility in all new vehicles.

Of the recalled vehicles, roughly 848,000 are in the United States, with an additional 107,000 in Canada, Mexico and other international markets. The recall covers a wide range of 2026 and 2027 model year vehicles across the company's Chrysler, Dodge, Jeep and Ram brands.

Which Models Are Affected

The recall includes the 2026-27 Chrysler Pacifica, Pacifica Plug-in Hybrid and Voyager; the 2026-27 Dodge Charger; the 2026 Jeep Cherokee, Compass, Gladiator, Grand Cherokee, Grand Cherokee L, Grand Wagoneer, Grand Wagoneer L and Wrangler; and the 2026 Ram 1500, 2500 and ProMaster, according to a filing with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.

"Drivers of affected vehicles should rely on driving in reverse the old-fashioned way — using side- and rearview mirrors — until an over-the-air update to fix the issue is available."

— Frank Matyok, Stellantis spokesperson

A Recurring Problem

The defect is not unprecedented for Stellantis. The automaker has issued several similar recalls in recent years involving radio software that disables backup camera feeds, including a 2024 recall covering nearly 1.2 million vehicles across earlier model years of many of the same nameplates.

The NHTSA adopted a rule in 2014 requiring rear-visibility technology in all new vehicles weighing under 10,000 pounds by May 2018, citing an average of 210 deaths and 15,000 injuries per year from back-over crashes. Children under five accounted for 31 percent of those fatalities, according to the agency.

Stock Impact and Industry Context

Stellantis stock fell 4.4 percent on Monday, pushing shares to an all-time low of around $5.12, according to MarketSurge data. The company's shares have declined roughly 50 percent this year.

The recall adds to an already difficult year for the automaker on the regulatory front. Stellantis ranks second among automakers for total vehicles recalled in the United States in 2026, with nearly 3.9 million vehicles affected as of August 10, according to Department of Transportation data. Only Ford, with 13.6 million recalled vehicles, has a higher tally this year.

What Owners Should Do

Stellantis said the fix will come via an over-the-air radio software update, and drivers will be prompted on their vehicle's media screen when the update is ready to download. The company said it is not aware of any accidents or injuries connected to the defect.

Recall notices will be mailed to affected vehicle owners beginning next month with additional instructions. Owners can also contact FCA US customer service for more information about the recall status.
